rows.jp: 世界は美しい。
rows.en: The world is beautiful.

ghs.en: The world is beautiful.

rows.jp: ここから街を眺め渡すたび、なにをとち狂ったかそう思う。
rows.en: Every time I look out over the town from here, some lunatic part of me thinks so.

ghs.en: Every time I pass my gaze over the town from up here, something that must be very wrong inside makes me think so.

rows.jp: でも美しいものはしょうがない。
rows.en: But beautiful is beautiful. What can you do?

ghs.en: But when something is beautiful there are no ways to deny it.

rows.jp: 青々とした夏の大気。
rows.en: The lush blue air of summer.

ghs.en: It's the lush atmosphere of Summer,

rows.jp: 一言で形容してしまうのが惜しいほど優美で。
rows.en: Too graceful to be done justice by a single word.

ghs.en: so gracefully elegant that to describe it in a few words is to disappoint it.
ghs.assessment: The source says the sight is so elegant that reducing it to a single description would feel regrettable or wasteful. The English instead says that description disappoints the object, adding an unsupported interpersonal relation and weakening 一言's compression to 'a few words.'
ghs.remedy: Describe an elegance too rich to reduce to a single phrase.

rows.jp: 峠からの眺望は、いつもそんな所感を抱かせる。
rows.en: The view from the pass always leaves me with that impression.

ghs.en: Those are the feelings that the view from this ridge always arouses in me.

rows.jp: ひそやかに息づく木々の合間からは、山々によって外界から隔絶された白い建物群が見えた。
rows.en: Through the quietly breathing trees, I can see a cluster of white buildings cut off from the outside world by the mountains.

ghs.en: From the break between the quietly breathing trees one could see a flock of white buildings, isolated from the outside world by mountains.

rows.jp: 街だ。
rows.en: The town.

ghs.en: It's a town.

rows.jp: 真新しく清潔、かつ閑静な地方都市……のはずれ。
rows.en: A brand-new, spotless, quiet regional city... or rather, its outskirts.

ghs.en:
A brand new, pure, immaculate, and quiet suburban
city... 's rear end.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes the outskirts of a brand-new, clean, quiet regional city. The English turns 地方都市 into 'suburban city,' renders はずれ as the anatomically comic and grammatically detached 'rear end,' and redundantly splits 清潔 into 'pure, immaculate.'
ghs.remedy: Identify the location as the outskirts of a new, clean, quiet regional city.

highlights.text:
A brand new, pure, immaculate, and quiet suburban
city... 's rear end.

rows.jp: つまりはしっこだ。
rows.en: The edge of it, in other words.

ghs.en: In short, this is just the appendix.
ghs.assessment: はしっこ means an edge, end, or fringe. 'Appendix' names an attached supplement or organ and is not an English equivalent in this locative context.
ghs.remedy: Call it the edge or outskirts.

rows.jp: 市の本体はというと、激険しい山を挟んで向こう側にある。
rows.en: The city proper lies on the other side of a ferociously steep mountain.

ghs.en: If one is looking for the main body of this city, it lies on the opposite side of these incredibly steep mountains.

rows.jp: ちなみに向こう側にはデパートもあり、時間さえかければ都心にも出られる路線がそのつま先を置き、レンタルショップはおろかゲーセン・本屋・飲み屋・出張（ヘルス）まである。
rows.en: Over there, incidentally, they have a department store. A rail line has even poked one toe into the place, and it will carry you into the heart of the city if you’re willing to spend the time. There’s a video rental store, an arcade, a bookstore, bars—even outcall sex services.

ghs.en: Speaking of this other side, there's department stores, and if one takes the time, the routes that lead to the city center will lay at one's feet rental shops of course, and game centers, and book stores, and even "health services" shops.
ghs.assessment: The source lists amenities on the far side and says a rail line reaches toward the city center if one is willing to spend the time. The English attaches the rental shop to what the route 'will lay at one's feet,' omits the drinking establishment, pluralizes and redistributes items, and converts an outcall adult service into ordinary 'health services' shops. The resulting syntax also obscures the list's structure.
ghs.remedy: Keep the rail-line clause separate and reproduce the full amenity list, including the drinking establishment and outcall adult service.

highlights.text: Speaking of this other side, there's department stores, and if one takes the time, the routes that lead to the city center will lay at one's feet rental shops of course, and game centers, and book stores, and even "health services" shops.

rows.jp: 飽食の極みを迎えた文明の、爛熟(らんじゅく)した果実がここにある。
rows.en: Here, then, is the overripe fruit of a civilization gorged to the limit.

ghs.en: There it lies, the over-ripened fruit of a civilization that welcomes the heights of appetite.
ghs.assessment: 飽食 is satiation or overabundant consumption, not appetite. The source characterizes a civilization that has reached the extreme of surfeit; the English reverses this into welcoming appetite.
ghs.remedy: Refer to a civilization at the height of overconsumption or surfeit.

rows.jp: 通称『都会』。
rows.en: Commonly known as ‘the city.’

ghs.en: Alias a City.

rows.jp: さて、こっち側。
rows.en: Now, this side.

ghs.en: So then, about this side.

rows.jp: 民家が山のようにある。
rows.en: There are houses by the mountainful.

ghs.en: There's residences, and mountains of them.

rows.jp: 山も山のようにある。
rows.en: There are also mountains by the mountainful.

ghs.en: Also mountains, and mountains of them.

rows.jp: あと学校がある。これは一つしかない。
rows.en: And a school. Only one of those.

ghs.en: And there's also a school. Just one, and no more.

rows.jp: 他に目立ったものといえば、大自然ぐらいのものか。
rows.en: The only other thing of note is nature. Lots of it.

ghs.en: As for other things that jump to the eye, there are only the things of nature perhaps.

rows.jp: 都会に傅(かしず)き、そのおこぼれで日々を営み、馬車馬のように働く人民を迎え、送り出し、時には生みだし（大人のジョーク①）、夜は優しくも高らかに眠らせあげるのである。
rows.en: This land bows before the city, lives off its scraps, welcomes and sends off the laboring masses who toil like draft horses, occasionally produces more of them (Adult Joke No. 1), then gently puts them to bed at night and lets them sleep with gusto.

ghs.en: Those people who work like horses, carrying on their days with the leftovers of the city they manserve, are here welcomed, sent off, occasionally brought into the world (adult joke #1), and put to very sound sleep at night.

rows.jp: 要するにベッドタウンだ。
rows.en: In short, it is a bedroom community.

ghs.en: In other words, it's more of a dormitory than a proper town,
ghs.assessment: ベッドタウン is the established Japanese borrowing for a bedroom community or commuter town. The English instead calls the place a dormitory and adds the contrast 'than a proper town,' which the source does not state.
ghs.remedy: Identify it as a bedroom community or commuter town.

highlights.text: In other words, it's more of a dormitory than a proper town,

rows.jp: 同じ市なのに。
rows.en: Even though it belongs to the same city.

ghs.en: despite being the same township.

rows.jp: 深い政治的事情がありそうだ。
rows.en: There must be some profound political reason for that.

ghs.en: Seems there are some deep political circumstances.

rows.jp: なお地図上では、二つの地を分断するこの雄峰、『丘』ということにされている。
rows.en: On maps, the mighty peak dividing the two halves is officially designated a ‘hill.’

ghs.en: According to the map, the majestic mountain ridges that cleave this territory in two are labeled hills.
ghs.assessment: The source points to this singular majestic peak, which separates two places and is designated a 'hill' on the map. The English pluralizes the peak into ridges, changes two places into one territory split in two, and pluralizes the map label.
ghs.remedy: Keep the singular peak, the two separated places, and the singular cartographic label.

highlights.text: According to the map, the majestic mountain ridges that cleave this territory in two are labeled hills.

rows.jp: どう見てもそんな可愛らしい代物ではない。
rows.en: It is not remotely that cute.

ghs.en: However you look at it, that is no sweet little affair.

rows.jp: 地図で見て文字通り丘と勘違いし、ワイフとマイサン引き連れてハイキングになど行こうものなら、家族ぐるみで遭難することうけあいである。
rows.en: Mistake it for an actual hill on the map, take the wife and Junior hiking, and the whole family is guaranteed to wind up lost.

ghs.en: Taking the word of the map literally and mistaking them for a hill, someone who's planning a wife-and-my-son hiking trip or something will then be met with a guaranteed family-wide stranding.

rows.jp: 都会との交通手段は、電車と未舗装の山道しかない。
rows.en: The only routes into the city are the train and an unpaved mountain road.

ghs.en: Means of transportation in and out of town are a train and an unpaved mountain trail, nothing else.

rows.jp: 一応、反対方向の峠まで行けば、道がある。
rows.en: Technically, there is another road if you go all the way to the pass in the opposite direction.

ghs.en: Technically, if you go towards the opposite ridge, there is a road.

rows.jp: ただし本当に遠回りになる。
rows.en: It is, however, an enormous detour.

ghs.en: However, in truth you'll just end up detoured.

rows.jp: それくらい無駄に距離がある。
rows.en: That is how gratuitously far away everything is.

ghs.en: There's little more than a length of pointless distance.

rows.jp: 田舎です。
rows.en: We live in the sticks.

ghs.en: 'Tis but countryside.

rows.jp: 以前、クラスの桜庭という男が、
rows.en: Once, a guy in my class named Sakuraba declared:

ghs.en: Some time ago, this guy Sakuraba from my class said:

rows.jp: 『このＮＥＷチャリで峠を制覇してみせる。これって、今の俺には必要なことだと思うから』
rows.en: ‘I’m conquering the pass on this NEW bike. It’s something I need to do at this point in my life.’

ghs.en: Sakuraba: 『I will prove myself by conquering the peak with this new bike. Because... I think that's what I need to do for my sake, right now.』

rows.jp: と歯を輝かせながら旅だったことがある。
rows.en: Then he flashed his teeth and set off.

ghs.en: And so he left for his journey, all while his teeth shined.

rows.jp: で。
rows.en: Well.

ghs.en: Then,

rows.jp: 桜庭は丸三日帰宅せず、警察の御出動と相成った。
rows.en: Sakuraba failed to come home for three full days, and the police were mobilized.

ghs.en: it came that Sakuraba did not return home for three full days, so that the police was formally dispatched.

rows.jp: 買ったばかりのマウンテンバイクを軽く試し乗りしようとしたらしい。
rows.en: Apparently he had only meant to take his brand-new mountain bike for a quick spin.

ghs.en: He'd sounded like he was trying to take the mountain bike he just bought for a little test ride.

rows.jp: が、調子に乗って隣町の相原市（超遠い）へあと五キロという地点にまで到達したところで故障。
rows.en: Then he got carried away and made it to within five kilometers of Aihara City—the next town over and absurdly far away—before the bike broke down.

ghs.en: But, getting carried out in the moment, he had a breakdown after getting to a point about five kilometers from the neighboring town of Aihara City (hyper far away).
ghs.assessment: The source says that after getting carried away and reaching a point five kilometers short of the distant neighboring city, the bicycle broke down. 'He had a breakdown' instead predicates a personal or psychological breakdown of the rider; the preceding 'getting carried out' also fails to express 調子に乗って.
ghs.remedy: Make the bicycle the thing that breaks down after he gets carried away and rides that far.

rows.jp: 車通りの少ない峠の道路を敗走途中、現行犯逮捕された。
rows.en: The police caught him red-handed while he was beating a retreat along a mountain road with hardly any traffic.

ghs.en: He was midway through his rout, on a mountain road with little traffic, when he was caught in flagrante delicto and taken into custody.

rows.jp: 桜庭の家はクラスメートの桐原と同じくらい金持ちで、親も過保護だ。
rows.en: Sakuraba’s family is about as rich as our classmate Kirihara’s, and his parents are just as overprotective.

ghs.en: Sakuraba's family is very overprotective, like the family of the about equally rich classmate Kirihara.

rows.jp: 西の桜庭、東の桐原と呼ばれる。
rows.en: Hence the saying: Sakuraba in the west, Kirihara in the east.

ghs.en: They get called Sakurabas of the West, and Kiriharas of the East.

rows.jp: 桐原は武士の家系で、その娘も貴族娘っぽい厳格な雰囲気。
rows.en: The Kiriharas are descended from samurai, and their daughter has the stern bearing of a young aristocrat.

ghs.en: The Kiriharas are of warrior lineage, and their daughter also has the stern air of the aristocrat's daughter.

rows.jp: 家族揃って苦虫を噛みつぶしたような顔をしていて、毒舌で、全体的に愛がない。
rows.en: The whole family looks as if they’ve just bitten into a bitter little bug. Caustic tongues, too. Not much love in the air generally.

ghs.en: Her relatives to a one have these sour faces as if they were chewing bitterbugs, the abusive language to match, and on the overall they are devoid of love.

rows.jp: 通称『ハラキリ』。
rows.en: Hence their other name: Hara-Kiri.

ghs.en: Common nickname: "Harakiri".

rows.jp: 桜庭一族は正反対におっとりとした一族で、父親は盲腸の痛みに気づかず死の一歩手前まで旅だったという武勲の持ち主だ。
rows.en: The Sakurabas are their exact opposite: an easygoing clan whose patriarch once failed to notice the pain of appendicitis until he had nearly embarked for the hereafter.

ghs.en: But the Sakuraba family was the complete opposite, a household of placid gentleness. His father had even accomplished the Feat of Arms of having voyaged to the brink of death by ignoring the pain of his appendicitis.
ghs.assessment: 気づかず says the father failed to notice the pain, consistent with the family's oblivious placidity. 'Ignoring' instead implies conscious awareness followed by deliberate disregard and therefore changes the comic causal premise.
ghs.remedy: Say that he never noticed the appendicitis pain until he was near death.

highlights.text: ignoring the pain of his appendicitis

rows.jp: その天然冒険魂は、確かに息子に継承されていたわけで。
rows.en: That blithe spirit of adventure has clearly passed to his son.

ghs.en: That spontaneously adventurous spirit would certainly see a worthy successor in his son.

rows.jp: 夜中になっても帰宅しない息子を案じて『誘拐されたんです！』と警察に駆け込むあたり、桜庭一族のまろやかな天然さが垣間見えて面白い。
rows.en: When their boy failed to come home by midnight, they ran to the police crying, ‘He’s been kidnapped!’ An amusing glimpse of the Sakuraba family’s mellow obliviousness.

ghs.en: It was funny to see a chink in the Sakurabas' naturally mellow nature when, in the dead of night, said son still had not returned and they anxiously stampeded off to the police shouting "he has been kidnapped!".
ghs.assessment: The family's panicked report provides an amusing glimpse of their mellow, guileless obliviousness. Calling it a 'chink in' that nature makes the behavior an exception or breach in the trait rather than an instance that reveals it.
ghs.remedy: Present the police report as an amusing glimpse of the family's mellow cluelessness.

highlights.text: a chink in the Sakurabas' naturally mellow nature

rows.jp: 桜庭は関係者に滅茶苦茶叱られ、自転車は没収された。
rows.en: Sakuraba was chewed out mercilessly by everyone involved, and his bike was confiscated.

ghs.en: The authorities reprimanded Sakuraba to the fullest, and his bicycle was impounded.

rows.jp: くわえて学校中の笑い者となった。
rows.en: He also became the laughingstock of the entire school.

ghs.en: And what's more, he became the laughingstock of the school.

rows.jp: 校内新聞一面の座を永らく独占し続けもした。
rows.en: For a long time, he held an uncontested monopoly on the front page of the school paper.

ghs.en: He kept monopolizing the top spot of the front page of the school newspaper for a long time.

rows.jp: 特にインタビューで奴が口走った内容が受けに受けた。
rows.en: His interview in particular was a smash hit.

ghs.en: Particularly, the specifics of what he said as he let his mouth run off during the interview made the rounds all around.

rows.jp: 『緊急特報！　蓮ヶ丈奥地に謎の人工建造物を見た！』
rows.en: ‘BREAKING NEWS! Mysterious artificial structure sighted deep in Hasugajo!’

ghs.en: Sakuraba: 『Urgent newsflash! In the deep lands of Hasugatake, a mysterious man-made structure was sighted!』

rows.jp: 『完全踏破12時間、秘境の奥地に隠された禁断のオーバーテクノロジー！！』
rows.en: ‘Twelve hours to total conquest! Forbidden supertechnology concealed in an unexplored land!’

ghs.en: Sakuraba: 『A full 12 hours of on-foot travel away, the most secluded backwood region is concealing Forbidden Supertechnology!』

rows.jp: 『長い道のりの果て、ここで我々はいまだかつて想像だにしなかった衝撃の事実を見ることになる！』
rows.en: ‘At the end of our long journey, we are about to witness a shocking truth beyond anything mankind has ever imagined!’

ghs.en: Sakuraba: 『And at end of this long voyage, we can there finally see a truth so shocking that its impact could never even be imagined!』

rows.jp: 無茶苦茶だ。
rows.en: It was unhinged.

ghs.en: Total nonsense.

rows.jp: 要するに奴は、帰宅の途中、道を外れて山に入ったわけだ。
rows.en: In plain terms, he had strayed off the road and into the mountains on his way home.

ghs.en: In short, this idiot, while coming back home, drifted into a mountain that's not connected with the road.
ghs.assessment: 道を外れて says that he left or strayed from the road and entered the mountain. The English instead describes the mountain itself as unconnected to the road, relocating the relation and adding a geographic claim absent from the source.
ghs.remedy: Say that he strayed off the road and into the mountain on his way home.

highlights.text: drifted into a mountain that's not connected with the road

rows.jp: おそらく近道目的だったんだろう。
rows.en: He was probably looking for a shortcut.

ghs.en: He probably wanted to try a shortcut.

rows.jp: そして偶然、とある施設を発見して大興奮した。
rows.en: Then he happened upon a certain facility and lost his mind with excitement.

ghs.en: And then, he accidentally discovered a certain facility, and became all excited.

rows.jp: インタビューはこの後も、凄まじい展開となった。
rows.en: The interview only grew more sensational from there.

ghs.en: After this, the interview became even more absurd:

rows.jp: 『秘密基地が』
rows.en: ‘A secret base—’

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "In the hidden base..."
ghs.assessment: The quoted fragment marks 'the secret base' with が as its grammatical subject. The English converts it into a location introduced by 'in,' and replaces the compound's conventional 'secret base' sense with 'hidden base.'
ghs.remedy: Keep 'the secret base' as the suspended subject of the quoted fragment.

rows.jp: 『衝撃の』
rows.en: ‘A shocking—’

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "...shocking..."

rows.jp: 『武装した兵隊らによって』
rows.en: ‘By armed soldiers—’

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "...because of armed soldiers..."

rows.jp: 『人類の常識を覆す』
rows.en: ‘Defying everything mankind knows—’

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "...the defiance of the conventional wisdom of humanity!"

rows.jp: 本インタビューで使用された単語ベスト５。
rows.en: The five most frequently used words in the interview:

ghs.en: These are the top five words, by frequency, in the interview:

rows.jp: 第一位『謎』22回%N第二位『衝撃』19回%N第三位『発見』17回
rows.en: First: ‘mystery,’ 22 times%NSecond: ‘shocking,’ 19 times%NThird: ‘discovery,’ 17 times

ghs.en:
#1 "Mystery"      (x22)
#2 "Impact"       (x19)
#3 "Discovery"    (x17)
#4 "Forbidden"     (x6)
#5 "Hair-raising"  (x4)

rows.jp: 第四位『禁断』6回%N第五位『戦慄』4回
rows.en: Fourth: ‘forbidden,’ 6 times%NFifth: ‘terror,’ 4 times

rows.jp: 校内新聞は、桜庭という美味なる獲物を骨の髄までしゃぶり尽くした。
rows.en: The school paper picked Sakuraba clean to the bone.

ghs.en: The campus newspaper suckled on the bones of the delicious game named Sakuraba until there was nothing left.

rows.jp: 桜庭は報道の残酷さを思い知った。
rows.en: Sakuraba learned firsthand how merciless the press could be.

ghs.en: Sakuraba understood with his flesh the cruelty of the press.
ghs.assessment: 思い知った means that he learned or came to understand the cruelty of the press, generally through harsh experience. The source has no body or flesh expression; adding one turns the idiom into an unsupported physical image.
ghs.remedy: Say that he learned the cruelty of the press the hard way.

rows.jp: その後、ストレスで腹を下して一週間ほど下痢をした（記事になった）。
rows.en: Afterward, the stress gave him diarrhea for a week. (They ran a story.)

ghs.en: Afterwards, his bowels loosened via stress and he had diarrhea for a week (this became an article).

rows.jp: 八日目の朝にはけろっとした顔で登校してきた（取材された）。
rows.en: On the eighth morning he returned to school looking perfectly fine. (They interviewed him.)

ghs.en: On the morning of the eighth day, he attended school with nonchalance on his face (inquiries on this were made by the paper)...

rows.jp: 髪を金髪に染めて（特集記事・異論反論オブジェクションのネタになった）。
rows.en: He had dyed his hair blond. (It became fodder for a special feature, ‘Dissent! Rebuttal! Objection!’)

ghs.en: ...and his hair dyed the color of gold (they became material for a special report with man on the street pros-and-cons interviews).

rows.jp: 以来、奴はずっと金髪ライフ。
rows.en: He has lived the blond life ever since.

ghs.en: Ever since then, the guy's lived the blond life.

rows.jp: きっと、新しい自分になる、という錯覚を己に課すことでストレスを克服したんだろう。
rows.en: Presumably, he got over the stress by convincing himself he had become a whole new man.

ghs.en: He overcame the stress by imposing his self with the deluded belief that he'd become anew, definitely.

rows.jp: ……これが元で金銀コンビなどと称されることになったわけだが。
rows.en: ...And that is how we eventually came to be known as the Gold-and-Silver Duo.

ghs.en: ...however, that's also how we came to be known as the Gold-Silver Pair.

rows.jp: 閑話休題。
rows.en: But I digress.

ghs.en: But I digress.

rows.jp: もちろん桜庭が見た外宇宙から来訪した超知的生命体が極秘裏に建築した施設というのは原子力発電所なわけだが、これは市民に豊潤なる富をもたらした。
rows.en: The facility secretly constructed by hyperintelligent life from beyond the stars was, of course, a nuclear power plant. It brought the people of this city lavish wealth.

ghs.en: Of course the structure built in great secrecy on the other side of the mountains by hyper intelligent beings visiting us from deep space that Sakuraba saw was in fact a nuclear power plant, which had brought about the abundant wealth of the locals.

rows.jp: 二束三文の土地が、みるみるうちに札束に変わった。
rows.en: Land once worth pocket change turned into stacks of cash before their eyes.

ghs.en: In the strike of the blink of an eye, this three pennies for two acres of a land was transformed into rolls of banknotes.
ghs.assessment: 二束三文 is an idiom meaning virtually worthless or dirt-cheap, not a literal price-to-acre conversion. The English invents pennies and acreage, while みるみるうち means visibly or rapidly rather than 'in the strike of the blink.'
ghs.remedy: Say that dirt-cheap land rapidly turned into bundles of cash.

highlights.text: this three pennies for two acres of a land

rows.jp: 近代化が進み、文明が開化した。
rows.en: Modern went and ized. Civilization got itself civilized.

ghs.en: Modernization progressed, culture got civilized.

rows.jp: 富豪が何人も誕生し、ビルが建ち、人が増えた。
rows.en: Tycoons sprang up, buildings rose, and the population swelled.

ghs.en: With everybody reborn a millionaire, buildings were constructed, and people increased.
ghs.assessment: 何人も says that a number of wealthy people or tycoons emerged. The English changes this limited group into everybody and adds literal rebirth, substantially exaggerating the distribution of wealth.
ghs.remedy: Say that several fortunes or wealthy magnates emerged as buildings and population increased.

rows.jp: 土地は安く、税金も安い。
rows.en: Land is cheap, and so are the taxes.

ghs.en: The land is cheap, the taxes just as cheap.

rows.jp: 電気代はタダだ。
rows.en: Electricity is free.

ghs.en: Electricity is free of charge.

rows.jp: だから街には無意味な照明が無数にある。
rows.en: Consequently, the town contains innumerable lights with no earthly purpose.

ghs.en: Therefore, there are so many useless lighting fixtures throughout town.

rows.jp: だからといって、ベンチにライトを仕込むことはないだろうに。
rows.en: That still doesn’t explain why the benches need built-in illumination.

ghs.en: Nevertheless, they didn't 'rearn' to build the benches 'light', didn't they.

rows.jp: 市はそのテーマを『癒し』と定めた。
rows.en: The city chose ‘healing’ as its guiding theme.

ghs.en: The township decided that its theme would be 'healing'.

rows.jp: 原子力発電所などというものを抱えている僻地が、いかにも掲げそうなお題目である。
rows.en: Exactly the sort of slogan an isolated backwater with a nuclear power plant would choose.

ghs.en: For a remote place with a nuclear plant nearby, that's a very empty slogan to hoist up.

rows.jp: 市役所に至ってはロココ様式のそれはもう耽美的な建物で、外観から内装に至るまで『汝を癒してやろう』という厳かな気概に溢れ、来庁者を萎縮させまくっている。
rows.en: City Hall itself is a decadently beautiful Rococo edifice. From facade to furnishings, it radiates the solemn determination to HEAL THEE, intimidating every visitor who crosses its threshold.

ghs.en: The city hall building itself was an extremely aesthetic building in Rococo style, that overflows from the exterior all the way to the interior with the stately fighting spirit of "How Thou Shall Be Healed!", so as to overwhelm anyone visiting there on official business.

rows.jp: ちぐはぐな土地。
rows.en: A land of mismatched parts.

ghs.en: What an incongruous land.

rows.jp: だから……居心地が良いのかもしれないな。
rows.en: Maybe... that is why it feels so comfortable.

ghs.en: Therefore... living here might just be very comfortable.

rows.jp: 壊れてしまった世界は、妙に親近感を抱かせる。
rows.en: A broken world inspires a peculiar sense of kinship.

ghs.en: A world split and broken that inspires an odd affinity in me.
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: 「いて」
rows.en: “Ow.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ow."

rows.jp: 軽薄な音がした。
rows.en: A silly little bonk.

ghs.en: A frivolous sound emitted,

rows.jp: 頭がかくんと傾く。
rows.en: My head tipped sideways.

ghs.en: my head sunk forwards with a thunk,

rows.jp: 首筋の筋がひきつって、ものすごく痛い。
rows.en: A muscle in my neck seized up. It hurt like hell.

ghs.en: and the muscles of my nape stiffened with indescribable pain.

rows.jp: 「……なんだよ」
rows.en: “What was that for?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...the hell."

rows.jp: 振り向けば、そこに少女が一人。
rows.en: I turned to find a girl standing there.

ghs.en: If I look over my shoulder, there stands, alone, a girl.

rows.jp: 「なんだ、女帝か」
rows.en: “Oh. The empress.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "My, it is the Empress!"
Girl: "..."

rows.jp: 「女王陛下にはご機嫌うるわしゅう」
rows.en: “I trust Her Majesty finds herself well.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The most pleasant wishes that this meeting finds You in good health, Your Majesty."

rows.jp: 片手をあげて挨拶する。
rows.en: I raised one hand in greeting.

ghs.en: A greeting with one raised hand.
Girl: "..."

rows.jp: エスプリのきいた言葉には、ウィットに富んだ返しがあってしかるべきなのだ。
rows.en: A line so rich in esprit deserved an equally witty reply.

ghs.en: To those words so rich in esprit, a retort wealthy in wit would be suitable.

rows.jp: 『くわ～っ、誰が女帝か～っ、馬鹿言ってんじゃないですわ、すわすわっ！！』
rows.en: Something along the lines of: ‘Whaaat?! Who are you calling an empress, you preposterous ass, I do declaaare—declare, declare!!’

ghs.en: Girl: "Gwaaa～h, whooo are you calling an Empreee～ss! You shan't say something so stupid, shan't shan't!!!"

rows.jp: そんなような。
rows.en: Something like that.

ghs.en: Like...

rows.jp: だが期待したような返答はない。
rows.en: But the expected retort never came.

ghs.en: But there's no reply of the type expected.

rows.jp: それどころか冷然とした怒気さえ感じられた。
rows.en: If anything, I could feel a cold fury building.

ghs.en: On the contrary, all I could feel was her cold-hearted wrath.

rows.jp: 「どうしたの、桐原。ノリ悪いよ」
rows.en: “What’s wrong, Kirihara? You’re not playing along.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "What's the problem, Kirihara? You're not getting into the spirit here."

rows.jp: 「もしかしてアレ？　生理っぽいやつ？」
rows.en: “Is it that? That time of the month sort of thing?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Could it be that thing? That biological-ish thing?"
ghs.assessment: 生理 in this teasing context specifically refers to menstruation or a period. 'Biological-ish thing' removes the referent almost entirely and turns a pointedly intrusive question into a vague abstraction.
ghs.remedy: Retain the euphemistic but unmistakable reference to a period.

rows.jp: 空気がどんどん重くなってく。
rows.en: The air grew heavier by the second.

ghs.en: The mood grows steadily heaver,

rows.jp: でも止まらない。
rows.en: But I couldn’t stop.

ghs.en: but I don't stop.

rows.jp: 「月桂冠」
rows.en: “Time magazine.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wreath of laurel."

rows.jp: 「黒須太一……」
rows.en: “Taichi Kurosu...”

ghs.en: Girl: "Kurosu Taichi...!"

rows.jp: 怒りの波動が膨れあがる。
rows.en: Her aura of rage swelled.

ghs.en: The wave of rage swells up and outwards.

rows.jp: 「赤飯」
rows.en: “Red Lobster.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Auspicious red rice."

rows.jp: 冬子……桐原の下の名前、内心ではバリバリ呼び捨て……の額のあたりがひきつった。
rows.en: Touko—Kirihara’s given name, which I used freely and flagrantly inside my own head—developed a twitch above one eyebrow.

ghs.en: Touko... that's Kirihara's first name, and in my mind I vigorously strip it of honorifics... began to have a contraction in the dead center of her forehead.

rows.jp: 「のぉっ！」
rows.en: “You widdle—!”

ghs.en: Girl: "'llyyy!"

rows.jp: 実際には『こんのぉっ！』と言ってる。
rows.en: What she meant was ‘You little—!’

ghs.en: In truth, she's saying "reallyyy!",
ghs.assessment: こんのぉっ is an angry, drawn-out この, roughly an incomplete 'you...!' or 'you little...!' It does not mean 'really.' The reconstruction therefore substitutes a different word and breaks the explanation of the clipped preceding cry.
ghs.remedy: Reconstruct the cry as a lisped or clipped angry 'you...!' expression.

rows.jp: 舌ったらずなのだろう。
rows.en: She still had a faintly childish lisp.

ghs.en: so that had to have been her lisp.

rows.jp: 彼女の特徴的イントネーションだ。
rows.en: It was a distinctive quirk of her speech.

ghs.en: It's her characteristic intonation.

rows.jp: 令嬢然とした冬子が、口調に未熟さを残しているのは、正直笑えた。
rows.en: For all Touko’s polished young-lady bearing, that trace of childishness in her delivery was honestly funny.

ghs.en: It honestly made me laugh how Touko, so like a proper lady, still had immaturity in speech remaining inside her.

rows.jp: と。
rows.en: And then—

ghs.en: And,

rows.jp: ごっ
rows.en: Thud.

ghs.en: Smack!

rows.en: “Guh?!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...g'fuh?!"

rows.jp: チンだった。
rows.en: Chin.

ghs.en: It was on my chin.

rows.jp: クリーンヒットだった。
rows.en: A clean hit.

ghs.en: It was a clean hit.

rows.jp: 避ける暇もなかった。
rows.en: I had no time to dodge.

ghs.en: It was too fast to dodge.

rows.jp: 拳に突き上げられ、のけぞるように顎先が天をさす。
rows.en: Her fist drove my jaw upward, snapping my head back toward the heavens.

ghs.en: Thrust upwards by the fist, the tip of my chin points to the heavens, the head thrown backwards.

rows.jp: ゲームっぽい架空エフェクトが、脳裏に踊る。
rows.en: A purely imaginary video-game effect flashed across my mind.

ghs.en: A videogame-like Imaginary special effect danced in my mind.

rows.jp: 「……撤収手伝いなさいよ」
rows.en: “...Come help us pack up.”

ghs.en: Touko: "...now come help take down the tents."

rows.jp: 低い声だ。
rows.en: Her voice was low.

ghs.en: It's a low voice.

rows.jp: これ以上ごねるなら今度は空じゃなくて地面にＫＩＳＳすることになるぜ。
rows.en: Keep arguing and next time you’ll be kissing the ground instead of the sky.

ghs.en: If you fuss anymore from now, next time it won't be the sky that you implement a kiss with, but the ground.

rows.jp: 暗にそう申しておられた。
rows.en: Such was Her Majesty’s unspoken decree.

ghs.en: That was the interwoven implication.

rows.jp: 「はい、テツダイマス（ガクガク）」
rows.en: “YES MA’AM. I’LL HELP. (tremble tremble)”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes ma'am, help I shall! (clatter, clatter)"

rows.jp: 無言で俺の耳を引いてキャンプ場に向かう。
rows.en: Without a word, she seized my ear and dragged me toward the campsite.

ghs.en: Without a word, my ear gets pulled as we head towards the camping ground.

rows.jp: 「あっ、あっ、いたいですーっ」
rows.en: “Ah, ah, that hurts!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ow, ow, that huuurts!"

rows.jp: 「殴った私の手も痛いわ」
rows.en: “My hand hurts from hitting you.”

ghs.en: Touko: "The hand I hit you with also hurts!"

rows.jp: 「それは心を鬼にして子どもを叱った母親だけが言っていいセリフ」
rows.en: “Only a mother who hardens her heart to discipline her child is allowed to say that.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That's a good line only for a mother who hardens her heart as she goes to scold her child!"

rows.jp: 「男手少ないんだから、キリキリ働きなさいよ」
rows.en: “We’re short on men. Get to work, chop-chop.”

ghs.en: Touko: "We have so few men helping, so chop chop and get to work now!"

rows.jp: 「働いたじゃないか、合宿中にたくさん……」
rows.en: “I worked plenty during camp...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But I worked, didn't I, throughout camp and lots..."

rows.jp: 「最後まで気を抜かないの」
rows.en: “Don’t let up until the very end.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Don't relax until the last moment, you!"

rows.jp: 「……ちょっとの休息も許されない」
rows.en: “...Not one moment’s rest.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...not even allowed a short break."

rows.jp: 俺は戦士か。
rows.en: What am I, a warrior?

ghs.en: What am I, a soldier?

rows.jp: 「桐原」
rows.en: “Kirihara.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Kirihara."

rows.en: “...What?”

ghs.en: Touko: "...what?"

rows.jp: 「合宿、来てよかったろ？」
rows.en: “You’re glad you came, aren’t you?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You're glad you came to training camp, right?"

rows.jp: 「（ぷいっ）」
rows.en: “Hmph.”

ghs.en: Touko: "(Pfui.)"

rows.jp: 無視された。
rows.en: Ignored.

ghs.en: I was ignored.

rows.jp: 会話はずまないことけたたましい。
rows.en: Our conversation was a roaring nonstarter.

ghs.en: A clamorously wild failure to enliven the conversation.

rows.jp: これでも今日は滅茶苦茶話している方だ。
rows.en: And this was still more than she usually said to me in an entire day.

ghs.en: And for all this, today's the day to speak out nonsense wantonly.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that even this counts as talking an extraordinary amount today, relative to their norm. The English instead makes today an occasion for speaking nonsense recklessly, misreading 滅茶苦茶 as the content or manner of speech and losing the comparative 話している方だ construction.
ghs.remedy: Say that, even so, they have talked an extraordinary amount today by their usual standard.

highlights.text: today's the day to speak out nonsense wantonly.

rows.jp: 今日みたいにかけあい漫才をすることの方が、むしろ珍しい。
rows.en: A rapid-fire comedy routine like today’s was the exception, not the rule.

ghs.en: It's rather rare to have days of comedic duets like today.

rows.jp: 「軽いあたま」
rows.en: “Airhead.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Empty-head."

rows.jp: 「はい？」
rows.en: “Excuse me?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "What?"

rows.jp: 「殴ったとき、空っぽの音がしたから」
rows.en: “It sounded hollow when I hit it.”

ghs.en: Touko: "When I punched you, it sounded hollow."

rows.jp: 「そろそろ脳細胞、分裂させておかないと、大人になった時につらいわよ？」
rows.en: “You should really start dividing those brain cells soon. Adulthood is going to be hard on you.”

ghs.en: Touko: "If you don't let your neurons undergo division but quick, it'll be harsh when you reach adulthood, you know?"

rows.jp: 「失敬だな。弁護士は通っとるのか？　ああん？」
rows.en: “Did your lawyer clear that slander? Huh?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, how rude! Do we gotta go by lawyers now? Well?"

rows.jp: 「ほんっと……疲れる……きみ……」
rows.en: “You are... so exhausting...”

ghs.en: Touko: "...you are... really... tiresome..."

rows.jp: 盛大にため息をつかれると、こちらも萎える。
rows.en: Her monumental sigh took the wind out of me too.

ghs.en: With a lengthy, exasperated sigh, this also withers.

ghs.remedy: Say that the grand sigh makes the narrator wilt or lose heart too.

rows.jp: 黙って連行される。
rows.en: I let myself be marched away in silence.

ghs.en: I'm escorted in silence.

rows.jp: 視線はついつい、高そうなワンピースをしっとりとまとわりつかせた臀部に。
rows.en: My eyes kept drifting to her ass beneath the damp cling of that expensive-looking dress.

ghs.en: Against my better judgment, my sight runs down her of expensive-looking one-piece dress coiling down to her rear.

rows.jp: 「水蜜桃」
rows.en: “What a peach.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "White peach."

rows.jp: 聞こえないようつぶやく。
rows.en: I muttered it under my breath.

ghs.en: I mutter as not to be heard.

rows.jp: 「触ったら沈めるから」
rows.en: “Touch it and I’ll sink you.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Touch it and I sink you."
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: ど、どこに？（ブルブル）
rows.en: S-sink me where? (shiver shiver)

ghs.en: I-into what? (shudder, shudder)

rows.jp: 「せっかく夏期休暇、一週間無駄にした気分よ」
rows.en: “What a waste of an entire week of summer vacation.”

ghs.en: Touko: "It was my precious Summer Vacation, and now it feels like I wasted a whole week of it!"

rows.jp: 「意訳すると、楽しい合宿も終わりかにゃー、って感じだな」
rows.en: “Freely translated: ‘Oh no, our wonderful camp is already over, meow.’”

ghs.en: Taichi: "To paraphrase, 'this fun training camp is comeowing to an ennnd!', that's what it feels, right."

rows.jp: 「……脳割れてるんじゃない？」
rows.en: “...Is your brain cracked?”

ghs.en: Touko: "Didn't your brain split?"

rows.jp: 割れてる。
rows.en: It was.

ghs.en: It was split.

rows.jp: 「俺は楽しめたけどね」
rows.en: “I had fun.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I managed to enjoy myself, though."

rows.jp: 「ふん」
rows.en: “Hmph.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Pah."

rows.jp: 「……楽しんだくせに（ぼそっ）」
rows.en: “...So did you,” I muttered.

ghs.en: Taichi: "...and you had fun too dammit. (whisper)"

rows.jp: 「な・に・か・言った？」
rows.en: “Did. You. Say. Something?”

ghs.en: Touko: "DID. YOU. SAY. SOMETHING?"

rows.jp: 「いいえなにも、サー」
rows.en: “No, sir.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "No and nothing, SAH!"

rows.jp: 一週間の合宿。
rows.en: One week at camp.

ghs.en: One week of training camp.

rows.jp: ほんの幾度か、彼女の笑顔を見た。
rows.en: I had seen her smile a handful of times.

ghs.en: And her smile I saw only a few times.

rows.jp: 憮然とした顔つきがデフォルト設定の冬子だ。
rows.en: Touko’s factory setting was a look of perpetual displeasure.

ghs.en: A disappointed face is in Touko's default settings.
ghs.assessment: 憮然とした here describes a sullen, displeased, or indignant expression, not disappointment. The English assigns a different emotional state to the character's default face.
ghs.remedy: Use 'sullen,' 'displeased,' or an equivalent default scowl.

rows.jp: 楽しんだに違いないのだ。
rows.en: She must have enjoyed herself.

ghs.en: But she had fun, no mistake.

rows.jp: だってテント張って機材並べて。
rows.en: We had pitched tents and set up all that equipment, after all.

ghs.en: After all, with all the tents spread and the machine parts set up,
ghs.assessment: 機材 means equipment or gear. 'Machine parts' narrows it to components of machinery, which the source does not say, and changes the image of equipment being laid out.
ghs.remedy: Use 'equipment' or 'gear.'

rows.jp: 合宿はまるで別世界みたいだったから。
rows.en: Camp had been like another world.

ghs.en: the training camp looked like an entirely different world.

rows.jp: 「いてててててっ！？」
rows.en: “Ow ow ow ow?!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "OwTchTchTchTch?!"

rows.jp: 耳を引く力が強まった。
rows.en: Her grip on my ear tightened.

ghs.en: The Pulling Power on my ear got harsher.

rows.jp: 林道を抜けて、広場に出る。
rows.en: We emerged from the forest road into the clearing.

ghs.en: Out of the forest path we come out to a wide grove.
ghs.assessment: 広場 is an open area, clearing, plaza, or field. A grove is a cluster of trees, so the English reverses the spatial transition from leaving the forest road and emerging into open ground.
ghs.remedy: Use 'clearing' or 'open area.'

rows.jp: 光が満ちる。
rows.en: Light flooded in.

ghs.en: The light is in the rise,
ghs.assessment: 光が満ちる means that light fills or floods the space. 'Is in the rise' is not an English rendering of that image and instead suggests an unrelated act of rising.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Light floods in' or 'The clearing fills with light.'

highlights.text: The light is in the rise,

rows.en: “Hey! You two slackers over there!”

rows.jp: 独特の声質。
rows.en: An unmistakable voice.

ghs.en: It's a peculiar tone of voice.

rows.jp: 我らが部長だ。
rows.en: Our esteemed club president.

ghs.en: It's the President of our Club's.

rows.jp: 「私は違います私は！」
rows.en: “Not me! I was working!”

ghs.en: Touko: "That is not what I am doing it is not!"

rows.en: “Ow ow ow! Running is dangerous! Especially for my ear...”

rows.en: “Right! Work, work♪”

rows.en: “This man...”

ghs.en: Touko: "Really this man..."

ghs.en: Running lightly,

rows.jp: 「まったく……」
rows.en: “Honestly...”

ghs.en: Touko: "Seriously..."

rows.jp: 冬子のため息が追いかけてくる。
rows.en: Touko’s sigh chased after me.

ghs.en: chased by Touko's sigh.

rows.jp: 二人で、みんなのもとに。
rows.en: Together, we headed back to them.

ghs.en: In a duo in front of everyone.
ghs.assessment: みんなのもとに marks movement toward or joining everyone. 'In front of everyone' replaces the destination with a static public position and changes the fragment's spatial relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Together, we headed over to everyone.'

rows.jp: 「おーーーーーーーーいっ！！」
rows.en: “Heeeeeeeeeeeeeey!”

ghs.en: Taichi: Heeeeeeeey!!!"

rows.jp: わけもなく呼びかける。
rows.en: I called out for no reason at all.

ghs.en: I address the crowd without a real reason.

rows.jp: 広場で機材の後かたづけをしていた五つの顔が、一斉にこちらを向いた。
rows.en: The five faces over in the clearing, busy packing up equipment, turned toward me as one.

ghs.en: The faces of the five who were tidying up the equipment in the grove turned my way in unison.
ghs.assessment: 広場 is the clearing or open area established immediately before, not a grove of trees. The repeated substitution reverses the setting while the five people turning together remains accurate.
ghs.remedy: Use 'clearing' or 'open area.'

rows.jp: 視線が集まると無茶したくなる。
rows.en: An audience always inspires me to do something reckless.

ghs.en: When sights gather on me crazy I wanna be.

rows.jp: シャツを脱いで裸になった。
rows.en: I tore off my shirt and bared my chest.

ghs.en: I became topless by taking off my shirt.

rows.jp: 「やだっ！？」
rows.en: “What?!”

ghs.en: Touko: "BUT NO?!"

rows.jp: 背後、お嬢が引きつるように叫んだ。
rows.en: Behind me, the young lady gave a strangled cry.

ghs.en: Behind, the lady stiffened with a shout.

rows.jp: 構わず裸で駆ける。
rows.en: I ran on, bare-chested and undeterred.

ghs.en: Uncaring, I ran around unclothed.

rows.jp: 乳首が風とコラボレーションする。
rows.en: My nipples collaborated with the wind.

ghs.en: My nipples enter in collaboration with the wind.

rows.jp: 五組の視線を感じる。ますます気が高ぶる。
rows.en: Five pairs of eyes were on me. My excitement mounted.

ghs.en: I feel the sights of a group of five on me. More and more my excitement grows.
ghs.assessment: 五組の視線 means five sets or pairs of eyes. 'A group of five' instead denotes five people or five undifferentiated looks and loses the counted paired gaze established by the preceding five faces.
ghs.remedy: Use 'five pairs of eyes' or 'five sets of eyes.'

rows.jp: 「俺を見てくれーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーっ！！」
rows.en: “LOOK AT MEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Look at me pleeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeease!"

rows.jp: 五つの顔が、表情ひとつ変えずに元の向きに戻った。
rows.en: All five faces returned to their work without the slightest change of expression.

ghs.en: Five faces return to their original direction without a single change of expression.

rows.jp: 連携ピッタリの超上級放置プレイ。
rows.en: Flawless five-way coordination in the fine art of erotic neglect.

ghs.en: Perfectly Coordinated Hyper Pro-Level Leave-It-To-Chance Sketch.
ghs.assessment: 放置プレイ is the comic idea of coordinated, expert-level neglect or ignoring someone, with プレイ carrying a play/scenario nuance. 'Leave-it-to-chance sketch' introduces randomness and a comedy skit, neither of which is present.
ghs.remedy: Use an image such as 'perfectly coordinated, expert-level neglect play.'

rows.jp: 「アハッ」
rows.en: “Aha!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ha-AH!"

rows.jp: 馬鹿馬鹿しくも、愉快で。
rows.en: Idiotic, yet delightful.

ghs.en: Silly and nonsensical, but pleasing:

rows.jp: ただ今だけが楽しくて。
rows.en: All that mattered was how much fun I was having right now.

ghs.en: it's having fun, just for the moment.

rows.jp: 合宿が終わる。
rows.en: Camp was ending.

ghs.en: The training camp is ending.

rows.jp: 新学期がはじまる。
rows.en: A new school term was beginning.

ghs.en: A new school term is beginning.

rows.jp: また日常がやってくる。
rows.en: Ordinary life was coming back.

ghs.en: Again normal days are coming.

rows.jp: 当たり前の明日がやってくる―――
rows.en: Tomorrow was coming, as naturally as ever—

ghs.en:
A perfectly ordinary tomorrow
is coming---
